newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums steady, arb to east beckons.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums steady, arb to east beckons.

text.p: A dispute over the record high delivery of the Nov IPE gas oil contract continued to stifle barge business on Wednesday while on cargoes interest shifted to a possible arb to the east, traders said.

"We are paralysed again," said one barge trader, referring to a standoff between the main long and short that has caused congestion in the Rotterdam region. "Everyone is waiting to see whether the product will stay inside the (ARA) zone."
Prices firmed on benchmark Dec IPE futures, which gained 75 cents to $217.75 a tonne on API stock figures that were mildly bullish for heating oil.
Two heating oil barges were done at Dec IPE +$2 for early December and a low sulphur diesel traded at +$12.25, both fob Flushing, around unchanged.
On cargoes, big Russians were offered at Dec IPE +$1 with others put at +$2.50/3.00. Prompt heating oil was Dec IPE 3/4 with German grade low sulphur diesel at Dec IPE +$15/17.

An eastern arb appeared opening slowly as Singapore gas oil gains on buying interest from China. NWE cargo premiums remain pressured by low buying interest, good immediate supply and restricted French consumption due to the truck drivers' strike.
